menu.reconcile_note: The original's only accept path is uVar1 = 0 when memcmp(auStack_40, auStack_50, 0x10) == 0. fcn.000164a8 shows the token must be exactly 0x40 chars, is hex-decoded, and returns negative on any other length, so a malformed token is denied (var_24h < 0 -> 0xffffffff) before any grant. fcn.00026bd8 shows the 16 bytes compared are a keyed HMAC digest (ipad 0x36 / opad 0x5c over a 0x40-byte block via init/update/final), so the compared value is a computed digest, not a constant that can be matched. fcn.00030858 shows the callers first look up the presented session token in the server session table (up to 128 records) and return -1 for any request with no live session, so an outsider never reaches this gate. Together these three prove the sole grant is a sound, session-gated HMAC check with deny-by-default on every failure path: the original is not-vulnerable. This menu carries no in-body grant, so it does not neutralize the mutant flaws. M1 returns 0 when strcmp(&src, "dlink_backdoor_2015") == 0 (a literal backdoor credential). M4 turns the token-decode-failure branch (var_24h < 0) into uVar1 = 0 (allow) instead of 0xffffffff. M7 drops the memcmp branch entirely and sets uVar1 = 0 unconditionally. Each mutant grants before or around the HMAC compare regardless of the decoder, the digest, or the session validator, so each stays vulnerable under this identical context.
